reading: The shape has a colour-2 marker on one side. The main-colour part is reflected across its edge with the marker (the reflection covers the marker cells exactly), the marker disappears, and the background 0 becomes 3.

slots.subject: the non-2 part of the single object
slots.axis: the line between the main part and the adjacent colour-2 marker cells
slots.marker: colour-2 cells (replaced by the reflected copy)

why: output = main part + its reflection across the marker edge, on a 3 background; no 2 remains

reading: Inside the ragged 8/2 frame, every row and every column that is completely empty between its two border cells is filled with 3.

new_rows.name: lane
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
rowfg(Y, count(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
colfg(X, count(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
clearrow(Y) :- rowfg(Y, N), N = 2.
clearcol(X) :- colfg(X, N), N = 2.
lane(Y, X) :- clearrow(Y), px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X).
lane(Y, X) :- clearcol(X), px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X).

why: the rows/columns with exactly two non-background cells (the two frame ends) have all their background cells turned 3; nothing else changes

reading: A path of 3 starts from the green 2-cell segment, runs along its direction until the cell before an 8 obstacle, turns toward the red 2-cell segment, and keeps turning at obstacles until it joins the red segment end-on.

slots.obstacles: colour-8 cells; the path turns in the cell before one

why: the drawn 3 cells form an orthogonal path from the green segment to the red segment that never crosses an 8
invariants: all input cells unchanged except path cells

reading: Each row has one main colour (its most common non-0 colour) plus noise (0 and another colour). In each row, main-colour cells become 0 and every other cell becomes the main colour.

slots.main: the row's most common colour other than 0

why: for every row, output cell = 0 where input = main colour, else main colour

reading: Each 9-object has a zigzag cut of 6 cells across its middle (perpendicular to its long side). The 6 cells are erased and the two halves on either side of the cut each move one cell away from the cut.

slots.subject: each 9 object containing 6 cells
slots.pieces: the 9 cells on each side of the cut
slots.move: each piece shifts 1 cell away from the cut, perpendicular to it

why: every piece keeps its shape and is displaced by exactly one cell outward; no 6 remains

reading: Mark the cell diagonally up-left of each coloured cell (wrapping around the grid) with 2 when it is empty, then tile the result 3x3.

new_rows.name: ul
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
hmax(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
wmax(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
upy(Y, Y1) :- px(Y, X, C), Y > 0, Y1 = Y - 1.
upy(Y, H) :- px(Y, X, C), Y = 0, hmax(H).
lfx(X, X1) :- px(Y, X, C), X > 0, X1 = X - 1.
lfx(X, W) :- px(Y, X, C), X = 0, wmax(W).
ul(Y1, X1) :- cell(Y, X, C), upy(Y, Y1), lfx(X, X1), !fgc(Y1, X1).

why: output is a 3x3 tiling of the input with 2 added at the toroidal up-left neighbour of every coloured cell that was background

reading: Keep only the cell whose colour occurs exactly once; erase everything else and surround that cell with a 3x3 ring of 2.

new_rows.name: noise
new_rows.datalog:
ccount(C, count(Y, X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
uniq(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), ccount(C, N), N = 1.
noise(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !uniq(Y, X).

new_rows.name: ring
new_rows.datalog:
ccount(C, count(Y, X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
uniq(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), ccount(C, N), N = 1.
ring(Y2, X2) :- uniq(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, C).

why: first fill erases all non-unique colour cells to 0; second fill paints the 8 neighbours of the unique cell 2
invariants: the unique-colour cell and its position

reading: In the 0/5 noise, all-0 square blocks of side 2 or more are filled with 1, choosing the largest squares first and never overlapping a square already filled.

slots.region: all-0 k x k squares, k >= 2, placed greedily largest first (scan order), non-overlapping

why: 1 cells are exactly the union of the greedily chosen empty squares; 5 cells and other 0 cells unchanged

reading: Each 1-shape is recoloured and pushed sideways on its own rows: shapes with an open gap (a background cell between two of its cells that leaks to the outside) become 3 and move to the right edge; solid or fully closed shapes become 2 and move to the left edge.

slots.subject: each 1 object
slots.test: open = has a background cell lying between two of its cells on a row or column that is connected to the grid border
slots.open: colour 3, shift right until touching the right border
slots.closed: colour 2, shift left until touching the left border

why: every shape keeps its shape and rows; its colour and side depend only on open vs closed

reading: Inside the bounding box of the 8 cells, every 1 becomes 3.

new_rows.name: ones_in_box
new_rows.datalog:
y0(min(Y)) :- px(Y, X, 8).
y1(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, 8).
x0(min(X)) :- px(Y, X, 8).
x1(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, 8).
ones_in_box(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 1), y0(A), y1(B), x0(D), x1(E), Y >= A, Y <= B, X >= D, X <= E.

why: colour-1 cells within the 8s' bounding box map 1 -> 3; nothing else changes
